objects.description: RAII-like helper class for creating and managing a simple lockfile for a given filesystem path. It tracks an internal locked state and, when a non-empty path is set, attempts to place a lock by writing host and PID info to a file. Not guaranteed to be atomic. Key operations: try_lock() to acquire, unlock() to release, is_locked() to query, is_stale() to detect stale locks, and locked_by()/locked_by_as_string() to identify the process recorded in the lockfile. Construction/destruction behavior is not specified here; locking is explicit via try_lock().
Alias type defined inside utils::Lockfile representing the recorded owner of a lockfile: a pair of hostname (std::string) and process id (pid_t).

functions.name: utils::Lockfile::is_locked
functions.description: Returns the current locked state of this Lockfile instance. Intended to be checked after calling try_lock() or unlock(). Does not imply a filesystem lock exists; when the path is empty, try_lock() sets this state without creating a file.

functions.name: utils::Lockfile::is_stale
functions.description: Checks whether the existing lock is considered stale. Details of how staleness is determined are not documented in this header. Likely inspects the lock file (if any) and the recorded pid/host to decide if the lock owner is no longer active.
requirements: Behavior depends on the configured path; if no path is set or no lock file exists, the outcome is unknown based on this header.

functions.name: utils::Lockfile::try_lock
functions.description: Attempts to acquire the lock. If a non-empty path is set, this will attempt to create/write a lock file that saves the hostname and pid. Not guaranteed to be atomic. If the path is empty, no file is created but the instance’s locked state is set to true.
requirements: If a real filesystem lock file is desired, call set_path() with a non-empty path before try_lock().
Do not rely on atomicity; callers must tolerate races with other processes.
The format of the lock file includes hostname and pid; callers that inspect it should expect that content.

functions.name: utils::Lockfile::unlock
functions.description: Releases the lock previously acquired by try_lock(). If a non-empty path was used for locking, this likely removes or updates the lock file; exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: Intended to be called after a successful try_lock(); behavior if not currently locked is not specified in this header.

functions.name: utils::Lockfile::path
functions.description: Returns the currently configured lock file path. An empty string means no lock file will be created when try_lock() is called.

functions.name: utils::Lockfile::set_path
functions.description: Sets the filesystem path for the lock file. When set to an empty string, try_lock() will not create a lock file but will still mark the instance as locked.
requirements: Set a non-empty path before try_lock() if a lock file should be created on disk.

functions.name: utils::Lockfile::locked_by_as_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing who holds the lock, based on data saved in the lock file (hostname and pid).
requirements: Requires a valid lock file at the configured path containing hostname and pid; behavior/format if the file is missing or unreadable is not specified here.

functions.name: utils::Lockfile::locked_by
functions.description: Returns the lock owner information as a pair of (hostname, pid) read from the lock file.
requirements: Requires a valid lock file at the configured path containing hostname and pid; behavior if the file is missing or unreadable is not specified here.

data_types.description: A string intended to represent a filesystem path. It may be empty, point to a non-existent path, an existing file, or a directory. No specific encoding is required beyond being a generic path string.

A filename referencing a file populated with arbitrary random bytes by the fuzzer. Callers typically open/read this path and interpret its contents according to their own formats. The filename itself follows a generic pattern; the interesting part is the file contents being random.

import os
import random
import struct
import sys
from typing import List

# This generator produces bytes that the fuzzing runtime will expose via
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to exercise utils::Lockfile path usage.
# Goals:
# - Provide realistic filesystem path strings: absolute/relative, existing/non-existing,
#   directories/files, with edge cases (spaces, unicode-ish, special names).
# - Provide plausible lockfile contents when FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME is read as a file,
#   containing hostname and pid text so locked_by()/is_stale() style parsers can find data.
# - Multiple concatenated entries so the fuzzer can consume several FUZZ_PARAM_* calls.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Format of produced buffer:
# Repeated records: [1 byte kind][2 bytes big-endian length][payload bytes]
# kind:
#   0x01 => path string (FUZZ_PARAM_STR)
#   0x02 => filename + file content blob (FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME)
# Payload for kind 0x01: UTF-8 path string bytes
# Payload for kind 0x02: NUL-separated: path "\0" file-content-bytes
# The harness typically maps FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to a temp file with provided bytes;
# giving both a path-like name and realistic content helps trigger code paths.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ABS_BASES = [
    "/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/dev/shm", "/", "/home/user", "/run", "/var/lock",
]
REL_BASES = [
    ".", "..", "./sub", "../up", "./.hidden", "build/out", "./lockdir",
]
COMPONENTS = [
    "lock", "lockfile", "app.lock", "pid.lock", "session.lck", "LCK..1234",
    "file with spaces", "unicode_π", "name,with,commas", "semi;colon", "colon:name",
    "dot.", "..dot", ".hidden", "NUL_not_allowed", "CON", "AUX", "PRN",
]
EXTS = ["", ".lock", ".lck", ".pid", ".txt", ".dat"]
SEP = "/"

HOSTS = [
    "localhost", "host", "worker-01", "db.example.com", "my-machine", "😀-node",
]

def _rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix absolute/relative, with chances for directories and nested components.
    if rng.random() < 0.55:
        base = rng.choice(ABS_BASES)
        parts = [base]
    else:
        base = rng.choice(REL_BASES)
        parts = [base]
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        comp = rng.choice(COMPONENTS)
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            comp += rng.choice(EXTS)
        parts.append(comp)
    # Sometimes choose just base or empty for empty-path behavior.
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        return ""  # empty path to exercise in-memory lock
    p = SEP.join(filter(lambda s: s is not None, parts))
    # Occasionally ensure ends with directory-like component
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        p = p + SEP
    return p

def _lockfile_content(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create content resembling "hostname pid" plus variations and extra lines.
    host = rng.choice(HOSTS)
    pid = str(rng.randint(1, 1_000_000))
    lines: List[str] = []
    fmt = rng.choice([
        "{host} {pid}",
        "{host}\n{pid}",
        "owner={host} pid={pid}",
        "{pid}@{host}",
        "host={host}\npid={pid}",
    ])
    lines.append(fmt.format(host=host, pid=pid))
    # Add some extra data sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(f"timestamp={rng.randint(1, 2**31-1)}")
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append("note=lockfile for tests")
    # Trailing newline variability
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        text += "\n"
    # Sometimes add binary junk to ensure robustness while staying mostly valid.
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        junk = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 16)))
        return text.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore") + junk
    return text.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")

def _make_filename_record(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Provide a plausible filename and content. Use a simple name; harness will map to temp file.
    # Make sure path looks file-like (not ending with slash) and is non-empty.
    base = _rand_path(rng)
    if not base or base.endswith(SEP):
        # Attach a filename
        fname = rng.choice(["lock", "lockfile", "file"]) + rng.choice(EXTS or [""])
        if base:
            base = base + fname
        else:
            base = fname
    # Avoid overly long paths
    base = base[:200]
    content = _lockfile_content(rng)
    payload = base.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore") + b"\x00" + content
    return b"\x02" + struct.pack(">H", len(payload)) + payload

def _make_path_record(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    p = _rand_path(rng)
    # Ensure variety including some simple known paths
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        p = rng.choice(["", "/var/lock/app.lock", "/tmp/app.lock", "relative.lock", "./.lock"]) \
            or p
    payload = p.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    return b"\x01" + struct.pack(">H", len(payload)) + payload

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = bytearray()

    # Decide how many records to emit. Ensure a mix of both kinds.
    n = rng.randint(4, 10)
    kinds = []
    # Ensure at least one of each
    kinds.append(0x01)
    kinds.append(0x02)
    for _ in range(n - 2):
        kinds.append(0x02 if rng.random() < 0.55 else 0x01)
    rng.shuffle(kinds)

    for k in kinds:
        if k == 0x02:
            rec = _make_filename_record(rng)
        else:
            rec = _make_path_record(rng)
        if len(out) + len(rec) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(rec)

    # Fallback: ensure at least one record
    if not out:
        out.extend(_make_path_record(rng))

    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for utils::Lockfile-related fuzzers.
# The fuzz stubs heavily use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and FUZZ_PARAM_STR for paths.
# We therefore generate buffers that can serve as:
#  - A path string (ASCII/UTF-8) for FUZZ_PARAM_STR cases.
#  - A serialized file bundle for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME cases, where the harness
#    points to a file containing random data. Since we cannot create files, we
#    instead focus on paths-as-strings that are interesting, and also include
#    plausible lockfile contents that the library might parse if those bytes
#    are written by the fuzzer runtime into a file.
#
# Format we emit (bytes): a UTF-8 path string, optionally followed by sample
# lockfile content separated by a NUL. This gives the harness a chance to use
# the first chunk as FUZZ_PARAM_STR and the entire blob as FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# file contents if it mirrors the bytes into a temp file.
#
# The lockfile is expected to store hostname and pid. Common simple formats:
#  - "hostname pid\n"
#  - "hostname\npid\n"
#  - JSON-like or key=val lines
# We'll produce several variants to exercise parsing paths.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

HOSTS = [
    "localhost",
    "ip6-localhost",
    "example.com",
    "devbox",
    "workstation-01",
    "ܔunicode-host",
]

DIRS = [
    "/tmp",
    "/var/tmp",
    "/var/lock",
    "/run/lock",
    ".",
    "..",
]

FILENAMES = [
    "lock",
    "lockfile",
    "my.lock",
    "resource.lock",
    "LOCK",
    "lock_12345.pid",
    "a" * 200,  # long name
]

SUFFIXES = ["", ".lck", ".lock", ".pid", ".txt"]

def rand_pid(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Typical pid ranges; include edge cases
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 42, 255, 1024, 65535, 131072, 2_147_483_647]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return r.randint(1, 500000)
    return r.choice(choices)

def rand_host(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(HOSTS)
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        base += f"-{r.randint(0, 9999)}"
    return base

def make_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = r.randint(0, 7)
    if mode == 0:
        return ""  # empty path case
    if mode == 1:
        # absolute typical lock dirs
        d = r.choice(DIRS)
        n = r.choice(FILENAMES)
        s = r.choice(SUFFIXES)
        return f"{d}/{n}{s}"
    if mode == 2:
        # nested path
        depth = r.randint(1, 4)
        parts = [r.choice(["tmp", "var", "run", "opt", "data"]) for _ in range(depth)]
        leaf = r.choice(FILENAMES) + r.choice(SUFFIXES)
        return "/" + "/".join(parts + [leaf])
    if mode == 3:
        # relative path
        prefix = r.choice(["./", "../", ""])
        return prefix + r.choice(FILENAMES) + r.choice(SUFFIXES)
    if mode == 4:
        # include spaces and special chars
        return f"/tmp/{r.choice(['res lock', 'res.lock', 'res:lock', 'res,lock'])}"
    if mode == 5:
        # very long path (but keep within buffer limit)
        longname = ("long_" * r.randint(5, 20))[:200]
        return f"/var/lock/{longname}{r.choice(SUFFIXES)}"
    if mode == 6:
        # unicode in path
        return "/tmp/🔒lockfile-π.pid"
    # random-ish safe chars
    letters = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789._-"
    name = "".join(r.choice(letters) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 40)))
    return f"/tmp/{name}{r.choice(SUFFIXES)}"

def make_lockfile_variants(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    host = rand_host(r)
    pid = rand_pid(r)
    variants = []
    # space-separated
    variants.append(f"{host} {pid}\n".encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
    # newline separated
    variants.append(f"{host}\n{pid}\n".encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
    # key=value style
    variants.append(f"host={host}\npid={pid}\n".encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
    # JSON-like
    variants.append(f"{{\"host\":\"{host}\",\"pid\":{pid}}}\n".encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
    # Add some random noise after valid header
    noise_len = r.randint(0, 64)
    noise = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(noise_len))
    variants.append(f"{host} {pid}\n".encode("utf-8") + noise)
    # Only pid or only host to test partial reads (still valid file content generally)
    variants.append(f"{host}\n".encode("utf-8"))
    variants.append(f"{pid}\n".encode("utf-8"))
    return variants

def assemble_buffer(path: str, file_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Emit: path\0file_bytes
    path_b = path.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    blob = path_b + b"\x00" + file_bytes
    return blob[:MAX_SIZE]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    path = make_path(r)
    variants = make_lockfile_variants(r)
    file_bytes = r.choice(variants)

    # Occasionally produce empty file content or pure random data to vary behavior.
    roll = r.random()
    if roll < 0.1:
        file_bytes = b""
    elif roll < 0.2:
        rnd_len = r.randint(1, 256)
        file_bytes = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rnd_len))

    buf = assemble_buffer(path, file_bytes)
    return buf
